scenarios.expected: SDK operations, overloads, queries and listener sequences retain the advertised Firestore contract in each sandbox topology.
Sign-in, current-user handles, claims, tenant changes and rules enforcement preserve each app's identity.
RTDB reads, writes, listeners and connectivity controls retain their declared semantics.
Storage bytes, metadata, Blob return shapes and download URLs survive the applicable transport and browser fallback.
Activated Messaging operations and observer delivery work through the selected sandbox owner.
Optional AI and diagnostics capabilities preserve activation and refusal behaviour without importing browser ambients into Node.
Direct in-page setup, identity and disposal remain available without a CLI or worker.
SharedWorker remains the default and existing replacement, Studio and app-deletion paths remain usable.
Special SDK values retain their types and project/database identity across requests, results, events and capture.
Write intent, transforms, dotted paths, merge options and undefined policy execute once and remain distinguishable from observed state.
Invalid payloads, versions, sessions, depth and size fail before dispatch without hanging unrelated consumers.
A normal SDK write in one browser is observed by another isolated browser using the same Node host.
Delayed or failed init and wrong-project discovery never create a fallback local store or an indefinite readiness promise.
Two processes targeting one canonical state directory have one writer; stale discovery and browser registration cannot replace its authority.
Connection-bound work cannot forge another session; explicit controls follow the declared admission policy.
Identity, mutation and cleanup follow per-consumer accepted order while another consumer continues useful work.
Loss before send, during execution and after commit rejects calls honestly; restoration ignores old generations and never replays an uncertain mutation.
Explicit deletion releases one app and prevents resumption; temporary loss does not delete it.
Physical loss, heartbeat expiry and explicit connectivity changes drain the applicable onDisconnect work once.
Reset/import advances ownership generation before data replacement and old operations cannot repopulate it.
Failed or interrupted boot, repeated close and restart leave no orphan runtime, writer, connection, listener or timer.
SDK reads after process restart recover every advertised durable service, checkpoint and identity field before seeding.
Disk failures, corrupt state, interrupted commits and reset/flush races preserve recoverable data and report committed-but-not-durable outcomes honestly.
Published remote, mobile/admin and MCP consumers use the same Node store without a browser peer or competing local writer.
Declared loopback, IPv4/IPv6, HTTPS/proxy and trusted-network routes identify the intended host and refuse unsupported deployment combinations.
History/incoming-event races, duplicate producer sequences, reconnect and reset retain explicit ranges and do not invent backend commit order.
Declared count/byte limits, capture deadlines, workload latency and owned-resource bounds hold with a stalled consumer.
Studio and the runtime chip inspect the actual host and expose current state, faults and permitted controls.
Packed installs outside the workspace boot, operate and shut down on supported Node runtimes with browser globals absent.
